images.title: Cities in two years
images.purpose: Show a small slice of the population table so students see the 2011 and 2001 columns and notice most cities grew.
images.composition: A clean table with a header row and four city rows centred on a white page.
exact_structure: A table of 3 columns and 5 rows (one header row and four city rows), thin #2B2B2B lines.
Header row: 'City', '2011', '2001', with the header fill teal #0072B2 and white text.
Row 4: Kolkata, 44,86,679, 45,72,876; the Kolkata 2011 cell is outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7.
rejection: any population number altered or the digits grouped differently
more or fewer than four city rows
images.takeaway: Reading across each row compares 2011 with 2001, and most cities grew while Kolkata did not.
images.description: A table of four cities with their populations in 2011 and 2001, Kolkata's 2011 figure outlined.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video.
images.teaching_notes: Read each row left to right and decide if the 2011 number is bigger than the 2001 number.

image_decisions.why: Reading the table is the whole concept, so a short slice of it makes it concrete.
